title: The ionic model
summary: Metals lose electrons and non-metals gain them to form ions held in a giant lattice by electrostatic attraction. Write ionic formulas and explain the properties of ionic compounds.

keyterms.definition: A positively charged ion, formed when an atom (usually a metal) loses electrons.
A negatively charged ion, formed when an atom (usually a non-metal) gains electrons.
The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
A giant three-dimensional arrangement of alternating cations and anions held by ionic bonds.
An ion made of several covalently bonded atoms carrying an overall charge, e.g. SO₄²⁻, NH₄⁺.
The ability of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond.
Enthalpy change to separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous ions; a measure of ionic bond strength.
The tendency of a substance to vaporize; ionic compounds have low volatility.
Ability to carry an electric current; ionic compounds conduct only when molten or dissolved, as ions are then mobile.
The simplest ratio of ions in an ionic compound, e.g. MgCl₂; ionic compounds do not form molecules.

questions.prompt: What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ and O²⁻: two Al³⁺ (+6) balance three O²⁻ (−6).

questions.statement: Metals tend to form cations because they lose their outer electrons.
questions.explanation: Metals have few valence electrons and low ionization energies, so they lose electrons to form positive ions.

questions.text: The ion formed by a group 17 element has a charge of ___.
questions.explanation: Halogens gain one electron to complete their outer shell, forming X⁻.

questions.prompt: Match each polyatomic ion to its formula.
questions.explanation: Learn these common polyatomic ions; their formulas are not in the data booklet.

questions.prompt: What is the formula of calcium nitrate?
questions.explanation: Ca²⁺ needs two NO₃⁻ ions; brackets show two whole nitrate groups.

questions.statement: An ionic bond forms when electrons are shared between two non-metal atoms.
questions.explanation: Sharing electrons is covalent bonding. Ionic bonding is attraction between ions formed by electron transfer.

questions.prompt: Which pair of elements is most likely to form an ionic compound?
questions.explanation: A large electronegativity difference (K 0.8, F 4.0) favours electron transfer and ionic bonding.

questions.text: Iron(III) sulfate has the formula Fe₂(SO₄)___.
questions.explanation: Two Fe³⁺ (+6) balance three SO₄²⁻ (−6): Fe₂(SO₄)₃.

questions.prompt: Order the steps in forming magnesium oxide from its atoms.
items: Ions attract and pack into a lattice
questions.explanation: Electron transfer creates ions; electrostatic attraction then builds the lattice.

questions.prompt: Which ion is NOT isoelectronic with neon?
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ has 18 electrons (like Ar); the others have 10.

questions.prompt: Why does sodium chloride have a high melting point?
options: Strong covalent bonds within NaCl molecules
Many strong electrostatic attractions between ions throughout the lattice must be overcome
questions.explanation: Melting disrupts a giant lattice of strong ionic bonds, which needs a lot of energy.
Ions are fixed in the lattice. Molten or aqueous NaCl conducts because the ions are free to move.

questions.text: Ionic compounds are brittle because displacing a layer brings ions of the ___ charge next to each other, causing repulsion.
questions.explanation: Like charges line up after a shift, and repulsion shatters the crystal.

questions.prompt: Which compound would have the largest lattice enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Lattice enthalpy increases with ionic charge and decreasing ionic radius; MgO has 2+ and 2− small ions.

questions.prompt: Match each condition of an ionic compound to whether it conducts.
questions.explanation: Conduction needs mobile charged particles.
Strong ionic bonds throughout the lattice mean they are hard to vaporize.

questions.prompt: Why do many ionic compounds dissolve in water but not in hexane?
options: Water reacts to form covalent bonds
Water molecules are polar and are attracted to the ions
questions.explanation: Polar water molecules surround ions (ion–dipole attraction), releasing energy that offsets breaking the lattice; non-polar hexane cannot.

questions.text: In the NaCl lattice, each Na⁺ is surrounded by ___ Cl⁻ ions.
questions.explanation: NaCl has 6 : 6 coordination: each ion has six nearest neighbours of the opposite charge.
Bigger ions and lower charges give weaker attraction; MgO (2+, 2−, small ions) is strongest.

questions.prompt: Ionic character in a binary compound increases as…
questions.explanation: Bonding lies on a continuum; a larger difference in electronegativity gives more ionic character.
